title: Common-field adjunction descent of fixed rational stages
statement: Fix the prime, coefficient closure, finite-field datum, schemes, morphism and RingStageAssembly A of [def-sf-ring-stage-assembly-data], with no absolute separatedness hypothesis. Given any RationalStageAssembly P over A [lem-sf-rational-stage-localization], there exists CommonStageAssembly A P: closed operations at every compactification, counit-normalized comparisons from the supplied rational operations under each common-field inclusion, identity left comparison on literal pair objects, inclusion shifts independent of compactification, and the common-transition equation sending the inverse source transition to inverse target transition followed by the supplied rational scalar q. The rational operations, their realizations and their scalar comparisons are fixed inputs, not existential outputs. The full representative-arrow normalization and rational-localization existence are not conclusions of this statement.

source.place: Construction 6.6; coefficient construction step 5, common-field pair descent of an already supplied normalized rational family only

proof.text: Use rationalCommonLeft and rationalCommonRight: the supplied q maps obey the published tensor associators, and counit transposition proves the supplied b maps coherent. The compatible actual finite units and counits explicitly construct rationalCommonAdjunction. These constructions preserve the supplied rational functors and scalar maps, without any existential selection of pair functors.

Apply exists_rational_common_exact_shifts to these fixed functors and this fixed adjunction. It supplies only their shift structures, exactness, the unit/counit shift squares, and common-inclusion shift structures chosen independently of compactification. The explicitly constructed right adjoint preserves binary products and zero morphisms, hence is additive by Mathlib Functor.additive_of_preserves_binary_products. Its left adjoint is additive by Adjunction.left_adjoint_additive. Assemble the closed Operation from those explicit functors and those shift structures.

Use the inverse canonical stage-restriction isomorphisms as q and b. Their components are identities on literal pair objects. The pair adjunction counit-component formula is exactly CounitComparison.counit after cancelling those identities; the split lemma supplies qShift and bShift. The endpoint inclusion shifts were chosen once, so shiftX and shiftY are reflexive equalities.

Evaluate the pair functor on the forward transition using its representative formula and coherence, and cancel the image of this isomorphism to obtain the inverse-transition formula. Transport across the published transition functor equalities. As the restriction q components are identities, this is exactly CommonStageAssembly.transition. This completes every remaining field of the original unchanged statement.
